sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Elizabethtown, KY?
sections.html:
Sellers in Elizabethtown work mostly with Hardin County offices, since the sheriff bills taxes and the clerk records deeds, while the city handles code and permit questions. The choice that matters first is the sale route: hire an agent, find a buyer yourself, or accept an as-is cash offer, each with its own timeline and repair burden.

The city is the Hardin County seat and the ninth-largest in Kentucky by the 2020 count. It anchors a metro area that stretches across Hardin, Meade and Larue counties and includes Radcliff, Vine Grove, Rineyville and the housing areas of Fort Knox. The metro area had 125,569 residents in 2020 and belongs to the Louisville combined statistical area. Elizabethtown is a home-rule class city under Kentucky law.

sections.h2: How big is the Elizabethtown housing market?
sections.html:
Elizabethtown added more residents than any of its three peers in this group: 31,394 were counted in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimates 35,448 for July 1, 2025, a gain of 12.9% over the estimates base. The 2020 count found 13,095 households in 14,076 housing units, with 7.0% of units vacant and a median age of 37.7. About 34.2% of those households were one person living alone, and 29.7% included children under 18.

Owners live in just under half the homes here, so rentals are a big part of the stock. Veterans number 3,152, the most of the four cities, and Fort Knox sits about 15 miles north. Rent at $909 is well under the Florence and Georgetown figures.

sections.h2: Where is Elizabethtown, and what is its history?
sections.html:
Elizabethtown lies in east-central Hardin County on Interstate 65, about 30 miles south of Louisville and 80 miles from Bowling Green. The Western Kentucky Parkway starts at the I-65 interchange here, and the Bluegrass Parkway runs roughly 105 miles east to Lexington. Elizabethtown Regional Airport (EKX) is the local airfield.

Colonel Andrew Hynes had 30 acres surveyed into lots in 1793, and the town was legally established in 1797 and named for his wife. Thomas Lincoln helped build a millrace here, married Nancy Hanks in 1806 and lived in a log cabin in town, where their daughter Sarah was born in 1807. The railroad arrived on June 15, 1858.

The Civil War reached the square on December 27, 1862, when John Hunt Morgan's cavalry fired more than 100 cannonballs into town. One ball was set back into the wall of the building on the public square after a rebuild in 1887. The Seventh Cavalry under General Custer was stationed in Elizabethtown from 1871 to 1873, and the general and his wife lived in a cottage behind the boarding house now called the Brown-Pusey House.

The population was 556 in 1860, 9,641 in 1960 and 22,542 in 2000, which means roughly two-thirds of today's residents arrived after 1960.

sections.h2: What jobs and climate affect Elizabethtown homeowners?
sections.html:
The climate is humid subtropical, so cooling systems and crawl-space moisture deserve a look before listing. Employment has a manufacturing and health care base. Kruger Packaging announced a 400,000 square foot corrugated-box plant in the T.J. Patterson Industrial Park, with about 150 jobs planned, and a September 2026 announcement added a converting line expected to lift capacity by about 25%.

In 2022 the Census counted $880.7 million of receipts from health care and social assistance, more than any other city in this group, plus $155.1 million from transportation and warehousing. Workers average a 20-minute commute.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Elizabethtown homes?
sections.html:
Elizabethtown Independent Schools operates Elizabethtown High School, T.K. Stone Middle School, Morningside Elementary, Helmwood Heights Elementary and Valley View Educational Center. Hardin County Schools serves part of the city limits, with Central Hardin High School and several elementary schools inside the city.

  • New Highland Elementary, Bluegrass Middle School and John Hardin High School carry Elizabethtown mailing addresses but lie in Radcliff.
  • Central Hardin High School is inside Elizabethtown and uses a Cecilia mailing address.
  • Elizabethtown Community and Technical College is in the city, and Western Kentucky University has a regional campus at Fort Knox.

Because mailing address and district can disagree, read the district and tax district printed on the bill before describing a house to a buyer.

sections.h2: How does the Hardin County Sheriff bill property tax?
sections.html:
Kentucky names the January 1 owner on the Hardin bill, wherever the house sells later in the year. The sheriff takes payment at 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101, by mail or in person, and online or card payments add a 2.49% fee. The office phone is 270-765-5133, option 1.

  • Discount window: the month of November.
  • Face amount: December.
  • 5% penalty: January.
  • 21% penalty: February 1 through April 15.

The sheriff does not take partial payments on a current-year bill, nor a prorated payment split between seller and buyer, so one side pays the full bill and closing settles the difference. Tax districts 03 (Radcliff) and 06 (Vine Grove) carry separate city tax payment details on the sheriff's site. Owners aged 65 or over, and owners totally disabled, may ask the Hardin County PVA (270-765-2129) for the homestead reduction. It comes off the assessed value, equals $49,100 in the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, and follows the person rather than the house.

sections.h2: What does an Elizabethtown seller owe at the deed?
sections.html:
The transfer tax lands on the grantor, at $0.50 for every $500 block of value written in the deed, with any part of a block counted as a full one (KRS 142.050). A house at the $245,900 Census median owes about $246. Before it accepts a deed, the clerk collects the tax. Foreclosure deeds, deeds between spouses and nominal-price deeds from parent to child are exempt.

For any delinquent bill from an earlier year, the Hardin County Clerk (270-765-2171) gives the payoff. Add your mortgage payoff and whatever the buyer negotiates after inspection.

sections.h2: What does Elizabethtown code enforcement look at?
sections.html:
The Code Enforcement Division handles property maintenance, zoning compliance, nuisance violations and unsafe conditions. Ask whether your address has an open file. For past additions, ask the Planning and Development department whether permits were issued.

Inherited houses need extra preparation. The deed must be moved to the heirs or signed by the estate's representative, so speak with the county clerk and a Kentucky attorney first.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Hardin County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Hardin County Sheriff's Office at 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101 in Elizabethtown takes payment by mail or in person, and card payments carry a 2.49% fee. A duplicate bill is available if none arrived by early November.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax does a seller pay on a $245,900 house?
faqs.a: Roughly $246. The state charges the seller $0.50 per $500 block of the deed value, and 245,900 divided by 500 rounds up to 492 blocks.

faqs.q: Who owes the tax when an Elizabethtown house sells in the middle of the year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is the name on the bill. The closing agent divides the year between buyer and seller, and a single party pays the full amount at the sheriff, who refuses prorated payments.

faqs.q: Is Elizabethtown in the Elizabethtown or Hardin County school district?
faqs.a: Both serve parts of the city. Elizabethtown Independent Schools runs its own campuses, and Hardin County Schools runs others, including Central Hardin High School. The district printed on your bill settles the question.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Elizabethtown house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer can take a house with open violations. Ask the city's Code Enforcement Division what is on file for your address so the contract can say who will fix each item.
